_note: Evergreen emotional football stories (general football, all-time). Story Research uses these as always-available fallbacks and surfaces one when its subject is trending in today's news. Every entry is a real, tellable emotional story: death, tragedy, resilience, controversy, comeback, dedication. Respect caution flags.

stories.name: Marc-Vivien Foé
stories.subject: Cameroon / Man City / Lyon
stories.story: Collapsed and died of an undetected heart condition in the 72nd minute of a Confederations Cup semi-final in Lyon, June 2003, aged 28. Lyon and Man City both retired the number 17.
stories.hook: As he stood alone in the centre circle, no one near him, his heart simply stopped.
stories.angle: A man at the peak of his powers, taken mid-match, with the number 17 left empty forever.

stories.name: Fabrice Muamba
stories.subject: Bolton Wanderers
stories.story: Suffered a cardiac arrest during an FA Cup tie in March 2012; his heart stopped for 78 minutes. He survived against all medical odds. 'Fabrice Muamba, RIP' had already trended before he lived.
stories.hook: For 78 minutes his heart did not beat, and the whole stadium prayed for a man who was already gone.
stories.angle: The night football stopped — and the miracle that he lived.

stories.name: Christian Eriksen
stories.subject: Denmark / Inter
stories.story: Collapsed from cardiac arrest during Denmark's Euro 2020 opener; teammates shielded him as he was resuscitated on the pitch. He returned to elite football with an implanted defibrillator.
stories.hook: As he crumpled to the grass with no one near him, his teammates formed a wall so the world could not watch him die.
stories.angle: Death on live television, and a comeback nobody thought possible.

stories.name: Davide Astori
stories.subject: Fiorentina (captain)
stories.story: Fiorentina's captain died in his sleep of cardiac arrest in a hotel the night before a match, March 2018, aged 31. Fiorentina and Cagliari both retired his number 13.
stories.hook: He went to bed the night before a game and simply never woke up.
stories.angle: A captain, a father-to-be, gone in silence — two clubs retiring his shirt.

stories.name: Piermario Morosini
stories.subject: Livorno
stories.story: Collapsed and died of cardiac arrest during a Serie B match in April 2012, aged 25, after a life already marked by the deaths of both parents and caring for two disabled siblings.
stories.hook: He had already buried both his parents and cared for his siblings — and then, at 25, his own heart gave out on the pitch.
stories.angle: A young man who carried unimaginable loss, taken mid-match.

stories.name: Antonio Puerta
stories.subject: Sevilla
stories.story: Collapsed from cardiac arrhythmia during a La Liga match in August 2007 and died three days later, aged 22. His son was born months after his death.
stories.hook: He collapsed on the pitch, walked off, and three days later he was gone — his son not yet born.
stories.angle: A boy of 22, a father he'd never meet.

stories.name: Abdelhak Nouri
stories.subject: Ajax
stories.story: The Ajax prodigy suffered cardiac arrhythmia and catastrophic brain damage during a friendly in July 2017. He emerged from a coma years later but with permanent damage; his family cared for him at home.
stories.hook: The most gifted boy at Ajax collapsed in a friendly, and the brilliant mind everyone adored never came back.
stories.angle: A generational talent frozen in time, loved fiercely by a family who never gave up.

stories.name: José Antonio Reyes
stories.subject: Arsenal / Sevilla
stories.story: The Sevilla and Arsenal winger died in a car crash in June 2019, aged 35. Sevilla mourned one of their own; tributes poured across the game.
stories.hook: The boy from Utrera who lit up the Premier League died on a motorway, only 35.
stories.angle: A hometown hero, gone too soon.

stories.name: Emiliano Sala
stories.subject: Cardiff / Nantes
stories.story: Died when the light aircraft carrying him to his new club Cardiff crashed into the English Channel in January 2019, days after his record transfer. His body was recovered from the seabed.
stories.hook: He had just signed the move of his life — and the plane that was taking him there vanished over the sea.
stories.angle: A dream transfer that became a tragedy in the Channel.

stories.name: Diogo Jota
stories.subject: Liverpool / Portugal
stories.story: Killed with his brother André Silva in a car crash on the A-52 in Spain in July 2025, days after marrying his childhood sweetheart and weeks after winning the Premier League. He left three children.
stories.hook: Eleven days after his wedding and weeks after lifting the title, a tyre blew out and took him and his brother.
stories.angle: A perfect life ended in a single second on a Spanish motorway.
stories.caution: Recent and raw — handle with care.

stories.name: Gianluca Vialli
stories.subject: Chelsea / Sampdoria / Italy
stories.story: Fought pancreatic cancer for years with grace and openness, remained a beloved figure in the Italy setup, and died in January 2023, aged 58. His friendship with Mancini moved a nation.
stories.hook: He faced the cruellest disease the way he faced defenders — head up, smiling, refusing to hide.
stories.angle: A striker's dignity in the face of death, and a friendship that defined a generation.

stories.name: Siniša Mihajlović
stories.subject: Serbia / Bologna
stories.story: Managed Bologna while openly battling leukaemia, coaching from a hospital and the touchline, before dying in December 2022, aged 53.
stories.hook: He was diagnosed with leukaemia and, days later, walked into his press conference and told the world he would fight.
stories.angle: A warrior who refused to stop coaching even as the illness took him.

stories.name: Robert Enke
stories.subject: Germany / Hannover
stories.story: Germany's goalkeeper hid severe depression for years, partly after the death of his young daughter, and took his own life in November 2009, aged 32. His death transformed how football talks about mental health.
stories.hook: The nation's goalkeeper smiled through every save while carrying a darkness no one could see.
stories.angle: The mask of the professional, and the silence that killed him.
stories.caution: SENSITIVE — suicide and child loss; handle gently, signpost support.

stories.name: Gary Speed
stories.subject: Wales / Leeds / Newcastle
stories.story: The beloved Wales manager and former Premier League great died by suicide in November 2011, aged 42, shocking a game that thought it knew him.
stories.hook: He seemed to have everything — and one morning, football woke up to the unthinkable.
stories.angle: How little we truly see of the people we watch every week.
stories.caution: SENSITIVE — suicide; handle gently, signpost support.

stories.name: Bert Trautmann
stories.subject: Man City
stories.story: The German ex-POW goalkeeper played the last 17 minutes of the 1956 FA Cup final with a broken neck — and won. He'd already overcome a nation's hatred to become a City legend.
stories.hook: He felt his neck crack, stayed on his feet, and kept saving — with a broken neck.
stories.angle: An enemy soldier who became a hero by refusing to leave his goal.

stories.name: Petr Čech
stories.subject: Chelsea / Czech Republic
stories.story: Suffered a depressed skull fracture in October 2006 and nearly died. He returned wearing the protective headguard for the rest of his career and remained world-class.
stories.hook: A knee to the head fractured his skull, and doctors said one more blow could kill him — so he came back in a helmet.
stories.angle: Playing on with your life one collision away.

stories.name: Ronaldo Nazário
stories.subject: Brazil / Inter / Real Madrid
stories.story: After two catastrophic knee ruptures that many thought had ended him, he returned to win the 2002 World Cup as top scorer — the greatest comeback a striker has made.
stories.hook: Twice his knee exploded, twice the world buried him — and twice he rose to be the best on earth.
stories.angle: The body that betrayed him, and the will that would not.

stories.name: Eduardo da Silva
stories.subject: Arsenal / Croatia
stories.story: Suffered a horrific open leg fracture in 2008 that was so gruesome broadcasters refused to replay it. He fought back to play again for club and country.
stories.hook: The tackle was so brutal the cameras looked away — and everyone assumed his career was over.
stories.angle: Rebuilding a leg, and a dream, from the worst injury the game had seen.

stories.name: Luke Shaw
stories.subject: Man United / England
stories.story: Suffered a double leg fracture in a 2015 Champions League match, endured years of doubt and criticism, and returned to score in a Euro final and star for England.
stories.hook: His leg broke in two on the biggest stage, and for years they said he'd never be the same.
stories.angle: From a snapped leg and public write-offs to a European final goal.

stories.name: Ryan Mason
stories.subject: Tottenham / Hull
stories.story: A fractured skull from a clash of heads in 2017 ended his playing career at 26. He rebuilt himself as one of the youngest coaches in the Premier League.
stories.hook: One header ended his career and nearly his life — so he chose to lead from the touchline instead.
stories.angle: When the game you love takes your career but not your purpose.

stories.name: Andrés Escobar
stories.subject: Colombia
stories.story: The gentle Colombian defender scored an own goal at the 1994 World Cup and was murdered days later in Medellín, aged 27.
stories.hook: He scored into his own net, apologised to his nation, and ten days later six bullets took his life.
stories.angle: Under a badge there is a beating heart — and the cruellest price a footballer ever paid.

stories.name: Roberto Baggio
stories.subject: Italy
stories.story: As a boy he promised his weeping father he'd win a World Cup and beat Brazil; 24 years later he missed the decisive penalty against Brazil in the 1994 final. 'Baggio died on his feet.'
stories.hook: As a three-year-old he promised his crying father a World Cup — and the day fate gave him the chance, it broke him.
stories.angle: The most beautiful player, undone by one kick, carrying a broken promise forever.

stories.name: Vinícius Júnior
stories.subject: Real Madrid / Brazil
stories.story: Endured repeated, sustained racist abuse in Spanish stadiums and refused to stay silent, forcing La Liga and Spanish society to confront it — 'It wasn't the first time, nor the second, nor the third.'
stories.hook: As the whole stadium screamed slurs at him, he stopped the game and pointed — because he refused to pretend it wasn't happening.
stories.angle: A young man forced to fight a battle no player should have to.

stories.name: Marcus Rashford
stories.subject: Man United / England
stories.story: Raised by a single mother who skipped meals so her children could eat and relied on food banks; he forced a UK government U-turn to feed hungry children in lockdown.
stories.hook: A boy fed by food banks grew up to make a government feed a nation's children.
stories.angle: From free school meals to feeding a country.

stories.name: Adriano
stories.subject: Inter / Brazil
stories.story: One of the most feared strikers on earth, he spiralled into depression and drink after the sudden death of his father, walking away from the top of the game to return to the favela.
stories.hook: The most feared striker in the world lost his father — and quietly let his whole career die with him.
stories.angle: How grief hollowed out a giant.

stories.name: Iker Casillas
stories.subject: Real Madrid / Spain
stories.story: Suffered a heart attack in training in 2019, survived, and had to walk away from the game — the World Cup-winning captain, mortal after all.
stories.hook: The greatest goalkeeper of his era felt his chest seize in training — and just like that, it was over.
stories.angle: When the body ends a legend's story before he's ready.

stories.name: Cristiano Ronaldo
stories.subject: Portugal / Al-Nassr
stories.story: Grew up poor in Madeira; his father died of alcoholism-related illness at 52, and in 2022 one of his newborn twins, Ángel, died during childbirth. He keeps their ashes together at home.
stories.hook: He carries a lost father and a lost son with him onto every pitch he walks.
stories.angle: The most famous man in sport, and the private grief behind the goals.

stories.name: Munich Air Disaster (Busby Babes)
stories.subject: Manchester United, 1958
stories.story: Eight Manchester United players and 23 people in total died when their plane crashed on take-off in Munich in February 1958, destroying the young 'Busby Babes'. Matt Busby survived to rebuild.
stories.hook: The most exciting young team England had ever produced boarded a plane and most of them never came home.
stories.angle: A generation lost on a snowy runway, and the club that rose from it.

stories.name: Superga Disaster (Il Grande Torino)
stories.subject: Torino, 1949
stories.story: The entire Torino team — the greatest side in Italy — died when their plane hit the Superga hill in May 1949. Italian football never truly recovered.
stories.hook: The best team Italy ever had climbed onto a plane and, in a single crash, ceased to exist.
stories.angle: An empire erased in an instant on a hillside above Turin.

stories.name: Chapecoense Air Disaster
stories.subject: Chapecoense, 2016
stories.story: A Brazilian club's fairy-tale run to a continental final ended when their plane crashed in Colombia in November 2016, killing most of the squad. The club rebuilt from almost nothing.
stories.hook: A small club chased the biggest night in its history — and the plane carrying its dream fell out of the sky.
stories.angle: A fairy tale that became a funeral, and a town that refused to let the club die.

stories.name: Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha
stories.subject: Leicester City
stories.story: Leicester's beloved owner — architect of the 5000-1 title miracle — died when his helicopter crashed outside the King Power Stadium in October 2018.
stories.hook: The man who made the impossible happen climbed into his helicopter after the match and never landed.
stories.angle: The heart of a miracle, lost in the sky above his own stadium.

stories.name: Justin Fashanu
stories.subject: Nottingham Forest / England
stories.story: Britain's first £1m black footballer and the first to come out as gay, he faced relentless abuse and rejection and died by suicide in 1998 — a story football spent decades failing.
stories.hook: He was brave enough to tell the truth about who he was, and the game punished him for it until he was gone.
stories.angle: The pioneer football abandoned.
stories.caution: SENSITIVE — suicide, historic homophobia; handle with care.

stories.name: Socrates
stories.subject: Brazil / Corinthians
stories.story: The philosopher-captain who led the Corinthians Democracy movement against Brazil's dictatorship, a doctor and a genius, whose life of excess ended in 2011 — he asked to die on a day Corinthians won.
stories.hook: He was a doctor, a rebel and a genius with a ball, who used football to fight a dictatorship.
stories.angle: The most intelligent footballer who ever lived, and the freedom he played for.

stories.name: Diego Maradona
stories.subject: Argentina / Napoli
stories.story: A god to Naples and Argentina who lifted the poorest people with him, battled addiction his whole life, and died in November 2020 — the world stopping to mourn its most human genius.
stories.hook: He gave the poorest people on earth a god to believe in, and spent his life being crushed by it.
stories.angle: The genius, the addiction, and a planet in mourning.

stories.name: Zambia Air Disaster (1993)
stories.subject: Zambia national team
stories.story: The entire Zambia national team died in a plane crash off Gabon in April 1993. A rebuilt side, driven by grief, reached the Africa Cup of Nations final months later — and won AFCON in 2012 in the same city where they'd perished.
stories.hook: A whole national team fell into the sea, and years later their heirs won the continent in the very city where they died.
stories.angle: A nation's team lost, and a promise kept two decades later.

stories.name: Freddy Adu
stories.subject: USA (former prodigy)
stories.story: Hailed at 14 as the future of American football and 'the next Pelé', the weight of impossible expectation and endless failed moves defined a career that never took off.
stories.hook: At fourteen they called him the next Pelé — and the whole world watched the promise slowly disappear.
stories.angle: The cruelty of being a boy carrying a man's legend.
